property_summary: After any sequence of calls ending with Collect(uint256), the value of c.MinSum() remains unchanged.
After any sequence of calls ending with Collect(uint256), MinSum remains equal to its initial value (0) regardless of whether Initialized() was called.
After any Collect call, MinSum is unchanged if the reference was unchanged (MinSum is only set in SetMinSum).
The MinSum state variable is preserved after a Collect call that does not revert, reflecting its last set value.
After any call to Collect with any parameters, the value of MinSum equals the value it had before the call.
The value of MinSum after a Collect call should equal the value set by the last SetMinSum call, which for the reference is the argument passed to SetMinSum, but for the bugged version is always 0.
After a Collect call, MinSum remains unchanged.
After reentrant calls through Collect, MinSum remains unchanged.
After any number of calls to Collect, the reentrancy guard idempotently ensures that locked_ is false after the call completes.
After Collect completes successfully, the value of MinSum equals its value before the call, regardless of the caller, amount, or lock time.
After any sequence of public calls ending with Collect, the MinSum state variable is unchanged from its initial value.
After a Collect call, the MinSum remains unchanged (equal to its previous value) regardless of the call's parameters.
After any Collect call, the public state variable MinSum must equal its value before the call, but the buggy modifier permanently locks it such that a subsequent SetMinSum call reverts.
After a successful Collect call, MinSum remains unchanged (equal to its previous value) regardless of the call parameters.
After any call to Collect, the value of MinSum remains equal to the value before the call.
After any sequence of calls ending with Collect, MinSum is unchanged from its value after the previous SetMinSum call.
A call to Collect can never revert if the caller's balance is at least MinSum and the amount and the unlock time condition is met.
After any sequence of operations ending with a Collect call, the MinSum state variable remains unchanged from its value before the Collect call.
After a Collect call that does not revert, MinSum remains unchanged from its value before the call.
After a Collect call (which may revert), MinSum strictly equals its value immediately before that call.
After any sequence of public calls ending with Collect(uint256), the value of MinSum is always equal to the last value set by SetMinSum (0 if never set).
After any sequence of public calls ending with Collect(uint256), MinSum remains unchanged from its value at the start of the test.

After any sequence of calls ending with Collect(uint256) and starting with Initialized, the value of MinSum is equal to the value set by a preceding SetMinSum call, regardless of reentrancy or other state changes.

After any sequence of public calls ending with Collect(uint256), the boolean return value of Collect (whether the transfer succeeded) is false if the caller's balance is zero at the time of the Collect call.
After any call to Collect, MinSum is unchanged from its value at the start of the call (i.e., it is only modifiable via SetMinSum).
After any call to Collect, the MinSum state variable must retain its value (either zero or the set value) if Initialized was called before.

If SetMinSum has never been called (or was called with the default zero), then after any Collect, MinSum must still be zero because the original SetMinSum sets it to _val while the buggy version leaves it as zero. The rule: when _am is zero, Collect should revert if MinSum is zero (since balance >= 0 and _am >= 0 but MinSum > 0 fails). Actually, the correct invariant is: if MinSum is 0 (i.e., SetMinSum never called), then Collect should succeed only when balance >=0 and balance >= _am and timestamp > unlockTime; but MinSum=0 always satisfies balance>=MinSum. So the difference is that the original SetMinSum can set MinSum to a non-zero value, while the buggy version always leaves it zero. Thus the property: For any valid _am, if SetMinSum was never called, Collect behaves the same regardless. Wait — the bug is that SetMinSum does nothing, so MinSum stays 0. The reference can set MinSum to a non-zero value after Initialized, but if Initialized is never called, both are same. The failing test should capture that MinSum remains 0 after any sequence. Simpler: After calling SetMinSum with some _val, if Initialized is called, then MinSum in reference is _val, in mutant it's 0. So call SetMinSum(x), then Initialized, then Collect(0). The reference contract's MinSum is x != 0, mutant's is 0. For Collect(0) to succeed, need balance >= MinSum. If balance >0 and unlockTime past, Collect in reference will revert because balance(>0) < MinSum(x>0)? Actually balance >= MinSum: if balance is small, might fail. Too complex. I propose: After SetMinSum is called with a non-zero value and Initialized called, the MinSum remains the set value in reference and zero in mutant. So we can check that after such calls, c.MinSum() != 0 in reference but 0 in mutant. So property: after SetMinSum(42) and Initialized, c.MinSum() == 42. The buggy version will have c.MinSum() == 0, which is different. So we fuzz over _val and ensure it's non-zero, and after the calls, assertTrue(c.MinSum() == _val). That will pass on reference and fail on mutant. However the test must work for all inputs: need _val != 0. Use vm.assume(_val != 0). Then drive calls: c.SetMinSum(_val); c.Initialized(); assertTrue(c.MinSum() == _val). That's it.
For any caller, after calling Collect with any amount, the stored LogFile address must remain unchanged.
After calling Collect with any amount, the value returned by SetLogFile (the address of the LogFile) must be the same as before the call.
The identity of the LogFile (the address returned by SetLogFile) is invariant under any call to Collect.
After any call to Collect, the address of the LogFile contract remains unchanged and equal to the address set via SetLogFile.
After any sequence of calls ending with a call to Collect, the LogFile address returned by SetLogFile never changes from its initial value of address(0).
After calling Collect, the contract's initialized state variable must be true.
After a call to Collect, c.Initialized() must equal the return value of c.MinSum() being equal to c.MinSum().
After a Collect call that succeeds without revert, the c.Initialized() getter must return true.
After any call to Collect, the state variable Initialized must be true.
After any Collect call, the Initialized() getter must return true.
After Collect is called with any amount, the Initialized state variable remains unchanged from its value before the call.
Collect should never change the Initialized state variable.
After any sequence of calls ending with Collect, the Initialized state variable is true.
After a successful Collect call that actually transfers ether, the Initialized state variable must be true.
After any call to Collect with a zero amount, the Initialized state variable is false.
Calling Collect should not change the Initialized flag from false to true.
After a Collect call, the state variable Initialized must remain false if it was false before the call.
After a Collect call, the state variable Initialized must still be false.
After a successful Collect call, the contract must not become initialized (Initialized must remain false).
After any call to Collect, the contract's Initialized() state variable must remain false if it was previously false.
After each Collect call, the unlockTime of the caller must be at least the previous unlockTime plus the lockTime from the Put call that set it.
After a Collect call, the caller's unlockTime is at least the block timestamp of the last Put call that updated it.
After a Collect call, the caller's unlockTime is at least the block timestamp of the last Put call that updated it.
After any sequence of calls ending with a Collect call, the caller's unlockTime is at least as large as the block.timestamp at the time of the previous Put call that increased their balance.
After a Collect call, the caller's unlockTime is strictly greater than the block timestamp of the previous Put call that set it.
After any sequence of calls ending with Collect(uint256), the caller's balance in the contract must be at least MinSum if the balance was originally above MinSum and the withdrawal succeeded.
After any Collect call, the contract's total Ether balance must be unchanged unless the caller's balance is at least MinSum.
For any caller, when Collect is called with an amount equal to the caller's balance, the caller's balance must be >= MinSum after a successful call.
After Collect, the caller's balance in the contract is at least MinSum if the call was successful
After any Collect call, if the caller's contract balance was less than MinSum before the call, the caller's balance must remain unchanged.
Collect(0) should never increase the caller's balance when the caller has no funds.
After a successful Collect(_am) call, the caller's balance stored in Acc must decrease by exactly _am.
After a Collect call that reverts, the caller's stored balance must not decrease.
After a Collect call that reverts (due to time condition), the caller's stored balance must not change.
Collect should revert when the current timestamp is strictly less than the unlock time.
Collect always reverts if the caller's balance is less than MinSum, regardless of other conditions.
After Collect is called with any amount, the caller's balance is always reduced by exactly that amount if the call succeeds (i.e., unlocks right after a Put).
After any call to Collect that does not revert, the caller's Acc balance is always less than or equal to its previous balance minus the collected amount.
After Collect reverts, the caller's Acc balance remains unchanged.
Collect never reverts when the caller's balance is exactly zero and MinSum is zero, regardless of unlock time.
